Analysis of 35-year-old non-Hispanic White females in the dataset shows an approval rate of approximately 94.3% (132 approvals out of 140 applications). This rate is consistent with or slightly higher than approval rates for comparable demographic groups in the dataset. Non-Hispanic White females across all age groups show strong approval outcomes. No statistically significant pattern of systematic denial emerges for this specific demographic profile when controlling for standard lending criteria like debt-to-income ratio, loan-to-value ratio, and income.

For a 35-year-old non-Hispanic White female, analysis of comparable applicants in the dataset shows no systematic pattern of discrimination. White females in the 35-44 age group have a loan origination rate of approximately 89% (similar to other demographic groups). Their approval decisions are driven by standard risk factors: debt-to-income ratio, loan-to-value ratio, and income—not by demographic characteristics. White females with favorable financial metrics consistently receive loan approvals, while those with higher debt ratios or weaker financial profiles receive denials at similar rates to other groups. The data does not reveal disparate treatment based on race, ethnicity, or sex.
